copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Tuesday, late-night UTC kickoff, brings Iraq and Norway together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the Iraq side, by +10.8pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

Public Elo rates Norway 220 points higher than the other side (Iraq 1540, Norway 1760). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Iraq to win at 18%, the draw at 17%, and Norway to win at 65%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Iraq to win at 8%, the draw at 15%, and Norway to win at 78%. On the Iraq side specifically the market reads 8%, which prices out at American odds of +1233. Compared against the model's 18%, that's the +10.8pp gap the Pick rests on.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Iraq the lower bound is 14%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +6.4pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the Iraq side.

News will move the prior. With kickoff 25 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. On a Pick this wide, it would take material news — a missing star, a tournament dropout, a venue change — to collapse the gap below the +3pp threshold; on the narrower side of the field, a single refresh can flip Pick to Pass. Either way, the Desk re-publishes after each refresh and does not recommend a trade.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Iraq a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +10.8pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: Iraq enter as the longshot — Polymarket prices their chances at 8%. The model rates them at 18%, a +10.8pp disagreement and one of our widest in this competition.
copy.title: Iraq v Norway · the model leans Iraq
